These diagrams explain the principles of the systems we study; they do not show measurement results. For enquiries about using these illustrations or other laboratory materials, contact [laboratory317@gmail.com](mailto:laboratory317@gmail.com).

## Multi-antenna communications

![Antenna array and directional transmission](../assets/research/wireless-en.svg#still){}

An antenna array directs signal transmission towards user devices.

## Polar coding

![Encoding transform for four bits](../assets/research/polar-en.svg#still){}

An example transform for four input bits; ⊕ denotes addition modulo two.

## LDPC coding

![Tanner graph: bits and parity checks](../assets/research/ldpc-en.svg#still)

A Tanner graph connects codeword bits to parity checks. Each square imposes a constraint: the connected bits sum to zero modulo 2.

## Multiple access

![Data exchange between a base station and devices](../assets/research/access-en.svg#still){}

Phones, laptops and sensors exchange data with a base station. Multiple access methods coordinate how these devices share the radio channel.

## Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces

![Signal reflection via an RIS](../assets/research/ris-en.svg#still){}

The RIS provides a reflected path between the transmitter and receiver when an obstacle blocks the direct path.
